title: Quasi-excellence from a G-ring and a quasi-excellent Jacobson quotient
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal contained in every maximal ideal of $A$. If $A$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and $A/I$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], then $A$ is quasi-excellent.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 4.1, printed p.4, applied by Theorem 5.1 Step 1 (1-3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-g-ring-quasi-excellent-closed-fibre] to this same ring $A$ and ideal $I$. Its ring is commutative, Noetherian and a G-ring, exactly as assumed here; its condition on $I$ is containment in every maximal ideal of $A$, again exactly the present hypothesis; and its quotient is the same $A/I$, assumed quasi-excellent. Its conclusion is that $A$ is quasi-excellent. No completeness, characteristic, dimension or universal catenarity hypothesis is required. This reuses an existing theorem with identical statement and does not introduce a new lemma.
